sections.content:
Gives you a basic understanding to Fixed Income metrics like yield, duration, convexity, etc. And some knowledge into some financial derivatives such as Futures, Swaps, Options, Repo, Caps, Swaptions, etc. Concepts are straightforward to understand as a 4000-level math course.

But dont expect you would benefit from any S&T/Quant Interviews after studying the course as it ONLY provides a brief introuduction to the products such as the payoff function and how we use it theoretically. It would be much better for the course if it teaches how trading desks actually applies the products.

Btw, dont expect you need any coding in it. I only used Excel for the entire course.
sections.teaching:
Tbh i skipped most of the lectures so I do not know how he teaches. but regarding to the lecture slides, it is difficult to understand as it is a bit unorganized. There is not enough connection between the motive behind each product (e.g. what are the risks exposure)

In terms of presentation, slides are mostly about how do we derive the payoff or how do we derive the pricing formula

sections.content:
As what the course title said, it's everything around fixed income. Roughly saying,
Bond pricing, duration, DV01 and convexity, arbitrage pricing of bonds, hedging methods with duration and non-parallel shifts against interest rate
Pricing of option (bond/stocks) with binomial tree model (CRR model), replication of options with the underlying assets (also the hedging methods), Black's model and Black's formula for option with proof
SOFR futures, CME derivatives, Repo, Interest rate swaps, caps and floors, swaption, total return swap
The materials it focuses would definitely give you a broader into fixed income area, which could be useful when you are applying relative jobs or interns. But one problem with the materials is that, you will not get in touch with some real-life application when you are going through the slides. I think it would be kinda confusing for some learners who wish to have real-life examples for understanding the concepts. Overall, this course still gives you solid overview in fixed income derivative, especially you could know how to really price them in math sense. You could expect more formula derivations or the intuitions than that in FINA 3203.
sections.teaching:
If you are a self-learner, please go FINA 3203.
Prof Wu is not really good at speaking out his thoughts. His english is not really good and it's pretty hard to understand what he said (the bad accent). Well, this should be fine if the slides are clear enough. And this comes the nightmare, these are the messiest slides i have ever seen. Just for examples, the symbols are not mentioned and come from nowhere, the highlights to some formulas or tree models look like kindergarten drawings. You have no clue what he's writing or what he is trying to tell. So, self-learners I think you should not take this course if this prof is teaching.

sections.content:
The content has not changed so feel free to read the other reviews.

It is pretty interesting, but I am a MATH student rather than FINA and I found the content way too complicated. It basically has little to do with math in my opinion and just has too many tedious proofs and algorithms.

Also, majority of the homeworks need to be done using MATLAB, Excel, and/or Python. Idk why the pre requisites are linear algebra and multivariable calc? Those two courses are absolutely irrelevant for this course.

Thankfully, as I will explain below, the course assessment is fairly kind. Also, the final is completely open book where you are also allowed to bring your laptops. He didn't mention anything about googling so I guess that was also allowed? (though its not really helpful in 99% of the questions)
sections.teaching: I can't comment too much about his teaching, but the notes definitely could have been better. I was able to self study, but it was not the easiest to do so compared to some other courses.
sections.grading:
20% Weekly HWs
30% Midterm (1 two-sided cheat sheet + laptops allowed only for Excel use)
50% Final Exam (open book + laptops allowed for anything except MATLAB)

Don't be fooled by the midterm past paper he might give you as the actual exam ended up being much harder and very different.

The content after midterm is way too hard and I would imagine the final mean would be very low (as mentioned in older reviews) if it wasn't open book this time around.

My scores:

Homework (%): ~18/20 (can't be bothered calculating the exact score as there are 10 of them but this should also be the mean)

Midterm: 29/40  (Mean: 24)

Final: 33/60 (Mean: 34)

Final score: ~67% --> B-

Final score was slightly above mean so maybe I should have gotten a B.
sections.workload:
Personally found the weekly homeworks very annoying as they keep taking up valuable time when important assignments or midterms for other courses come around.

However, they are helpful for studying for the exams and are also a good chunk of the overall grade so you can guarantee a pass even before the final. Would still prefer longer but fewer assignments.

sections.content:
refer to others' posts
If you have taken MATH 4514 before the course, then pre-midterm content would be easy for you.

However, concepts of financial products related to Black's Model (eg. cap, floor, swaption...) are quite difficult and may need more time to digest.
sections.teaching:
Prof. Wu is a lovely and considerate professor.
He is approachable and helpful in answering your questions after class / via emails or during tutorial sessions. If you feel confused about the concepts, just schedule a meeting with him and clarify your doubts.

I agree that sometimes his lecture notes may jump too fast to the conclusion and students may feel confused. However, it's not a big problem as long as you CLARIFY YOUR DOUBTS with him.

He's an investor in the financial markets as well so he touches on some market events (e.g. FED FOMC, rate hikes, US stock market moves) during classes, too, to give students some color on how macroeconomic policy changes impact the fixed income products + respective hedging strategies.

I think he's underrated... Lol. Perhaps I have a different learning mindset from the others...
sections.grading:
Very lenient. Many students scored horribly low so Prof. Wu adjusted the grading policy otherwise there would be too many F-grade students.

Many students (like 75%) skipped his classes & tutorials. Only around 20 ppl showed up in his lectures.

I genuinely find fixed-income derivatives (or global markets, generally) interesting so I attended almost every class & tutorial sessions (except those clashing with my superday interviews).

Some exam questions are designed to differentiate A-range students from others with concepts that have been stressed repeatedly in class.

For me:
hw: nearly full marks
midterm: 20/20 (high 20/20, low 4/20, mean 13.2)
final: 38/50 (high 44/50, low 3/50, mean 19.58)

final grade: A+

Not majoring in MATH or MAEC but the course grade was quite good.
sections.workload:
Fair. The weekly assignments were effective in helping me learn the concepts.

My advice:
ask questions to clarify the concepts or read the textbook (it's available on HKUST library's online access) or Google the concepts

Introduction to financial markets

Term Structure of Interest Rate:

Note that Kr01, Caps, Floors is not taught this sem

If you have study MATH2511/4512, the first half of the course is easy. The materials for the term structure of interest rates is just a more detail version in those two courses. In this course, don't expect that the interest is fixed (as this is a fixed income course: By prof.) The interest rate curves are determined by market information (T-Bonds, Zero-Coupon Bonds, Par Bonds and LIBOR).

The second half is much harder than the first part. it takes some time to understand the concepts if you are a MATH student.

Basic Programming knowledge will be expected, Professor will use MatLab to demonstrate some concepts in the second half of this course.

This course is not Math heavy, you just need to have some basic knowledge in probability (CLT, Binomial and Normal Distributions)  and partial derivatives to understand the derivation of the formulae, others are just simply algebras (nothing about matrix operations). Stochastic Calculus is not needed for this course.

sections.content:
I like the content very much, since I like financial maths.

On or before midterm exam:
1. Term structures, spot rates, spot price
2. Bond Valuation, in 4511, Redemption value = Face Value, clean and dirty price
3. Yield rate, annual effective/ nominal, compounded continuously etc
4. Interest rate valuation and bond valuation, modified duration, convexity
5. Floating Rate Bond, Forward rate, FRA and currency forwards.
6. Interest rate swap

After Midterm Exam:
1. Currency Swap, Foreign Currency Swap
2. Options, European and American( just an introduction), call and put, bond call and put option, Put Call Parity and Convexity Property
3. More advanced on options: Callable Bond, Puttable Bond, Caplet, Floorlet, Cap, Floor and Swaption
4. Valuation on European Options: Binomial Tree Models, Risk Neutral Probability, Arrow Security...

As I also study FINA 3203, I will do a comparison.

Similar:
1. Similar syllabus, spot price, forward contracts, FRA, swaps and options and binomial tree model, Arrow Security (also called Binary Options in FINA 3203)
2. Test your brain, e.g. construct arbitrage opportunity, hedge risk

Differences:
1. MATH 4511 teaches caplet, floorlet and swaption while FINA 3203 does not; FINA 3203 teaches futures, American Option (more details), Black Scholes Merton Model, Exotic Options and Credit Spread and Default Probability; I think those things will be covered in MATH 4514.
2. FINA 3203 always assumes interest rate compounded continuously while MATH 4511 does not.
3. FINA 3203 tests more on your Economics knowledge than Math computation, while MATH 4511 tests you more on your brain, or tricks to solve the problems, both courses are very good.

Conclusion: I like both courses, if you want to work on this field in future, you should not miss these two courses. Reminder, Math students should take MATH 4514 instead of FINA 3203/

sections.teaching:
Although attendance is not required for this course, it is beneficial for you to attend his lectures. If you are good at Maths, then the lecture notes itself is sufficient for you to understand the materials (because it is just too neat and good). However, you may need to avoid sitting at the backrow, since you will not be able hear his voice clearly (and you will easily lose focus on the lecture).

*Spoiler alert: If majority of class attend the lecture, then it can almost be certain that your exams are not hard, just the matter of speed );
sections.grading:
1. Assignments (15% + Mystery Bonus Score)
2. Midterm Exam (25%)
3. Final Exam (60%)

Remarks:
1. As usual, the grading system adopted by Dr. LCM is "absolute grading", in spite of the fact that 117 students are enrolled into this course.

2. There are 3 assignments throughout the term, equally weighted (i.e. each assignment worth 5%).
For assignment 1, there are 60 bonus marks (+5)
For assignment 2, there are 70 bonus marks (+10)
For assignment 3, there are 85 bonus marks (+15)
* You will obtain the bonus marks (in brackets) depending on how much details you provide in each problems, and also on the clarity of the solution.
* If you do all 3 assignment seriously, you can obtain a maximum of 245 bonus marks, which can be used to top-up your midterm score (with 1 midterm score = 8 bonus marks) and also your final score (with 1 final score = 15 bonus marks, if you get 100 in the midterm after the top-up).

3. For the midterm exam, I myself find it quite hard. This is because people who has not learned about "no-arbitrage pricing principle" will find it confusing at first. There are 4 computational questions in the midterm (with 1 harder problem), with 75 minutes allowed.
* The problems are closely related to lecture notes, assignment (especially bonus problem) and problem set. Thus, pay more attention and try to get enough exercise before the exam.

4. Final exam... speed contest! 9 problems, all standard ones, and is basically the same as the midterm. Don't forget to stretch your hand and brain before the exam because it is going to be super TIRING.
sections.workload:
Basically, you need to put more emphasis on completing the assignments. I myself needed almost 3 days (3 * 9 hours) to complete them. But once you understand how to do the problems in each assignments, then it's just the matter of revision before the midterm and finals.

The workload is big, but it will pay off!

sections.content: The content is useful but is not really well organized. The notes and the homework have a lot of typo. And when he changes the contents, he won't email you. You need to find out yourself.
sections.teaching: The professor doesn't seem to prepare for classes. It is really confusing for everyone and sometimes confusing for himself as well.
sections.grading: The mean is around 70% and if you cannot get a overall score much larger than mean, you will get a B range.
sections.workload: the workload is ok but you really need to work hard to learn it yourself.

sections.content:
You should learn Fina3000s courses first before you take this course.
All maths-sf students are struggling to catch up the materials that fina or quantitative finance students already have known. Maths doesnt matter in this course. you just need to have a bit of understanding on stats.
sections.teaching:
Very bad.
I dont know why he kept explaining on unimportant materials on final or midterm. There are too many mistakes on his lecture notes.
you should be careful when you revise them.
sections.grading: grading would not be really expexted.

hw total 9, quiz total 4, midterm and final.

sections.content:
Introduction to financial markets

內容嚟講都算okay既，唔需要太高數學程度，但係會有好多formulae需要去記。
sections.teaching:
從未見過咁垃__既professor。
開頭第一堂講唔要求大家financial backgroud，結果講到option嗰陣又話你地應該take咗MATH 4512先。咁其實要求有底無問題，你開宗明義講咗先，又或者prerequisite寫明囉，咁樣反反覆覆真係難以苟同。
佢教得差全世界都知既，有啲professor係research叻既大家都明白，都係自修啫。
但係佢啲lecture notes永遠上堂前1個鐘先post，仲要係9點堂，就算我唔睇一次你都俾時間我print啦。
去到中段佢會1日前post，可以print出嚟啦，然後上堂發現佢改過曬啲野，咁我print嚟做乜。
都唔緊要啦，結果份notes成日出錯，講到邊改到邊。1份notes可以前後有3個versions既professor真係第一次見。
好啦有野唔明，咁office hour去揾佢啦，佢只會帶你遊花園，問完問題個答案係牛頭不對馬嘴。
Homework answer又要自己email TA攞答案，佢話驚人放上網之後搞到佢要改homework問題。懷疑太多人問TA逐個逐個覆覺得麻煩，最後TA都係選擇po上網俾大家睇。
不過好彩TA教得好，上tuto學到既野絕對多過lecture，如果唔係TA我完全唔知今個sem學咗啲咩。

sections.content:
Mid term: currency forward, call/put options and strategies, arbitrage pricing, spot & swap & forward rate, forward rate agreement and DV01.

Final: DV01, Duration, Convexity, key rate shift, Binomial model for interest rate, Eurodollar Future, Black–Scholes model.

Though it is not cumulative, there are a lot to cover in each exam.
sections.teaching:
Prof and teaching material are very poor. Prof seems not certain about the concept he teaches as he sometimes correct himself immediately after explaining something.

Teaching material can mess you up. The organization of the chapters are poor that you may find similar slides many times in different chapters. It makes the course hard to follow and I spend so much time to organize those concepts.

While the TA is helpful and patient, the tutorial notes are far easier to follow and I mostly use the notes to study. It is encouraged to attend tutorials. Whenever we have questions, he is so keen to answer.
sections.grading:
6 HW : 10%
4 quizzes: 10%
1 mid term: 30%
1 final : 50%

Poor but seemingly better than other math courses. Got below mean in mid term (maybe half sd?) and had no stat for final. The grade turned out to be a C. I guess the mean should be C+?
sections.workload: It is encouraged to spend time reading the slides after each class and make notes so that it's easier to follow. Also, attending tutorials could help you organize the concepts so it is better to do it.

sections.content: The course covers forwards, futures, options, bonds, bond options, swaps, swaptions etc. Focus is put on calculations of different rates and prices of the above derivatives. Initially the content may look familiar if you have studied financial derivatives before, but the concepts are put into mathematical context (e.g. formulas). It grows a lot more difficult when it goes into topics of rates and bond options. Thorough understanding of the concepts is needed to perform well in the exams, since it involves many proofs rather than plain calculations.
sections.teaching: Both the powerpoint slides and professor's teaching in class are poorly organized. Most of the time people don't pay attention since the professor speaks at monotone and people find it difficult to understand what he tried to say. No attendance counted so many people did not go to class when the semester reaches its end.
sections.grading:
10% Homework
10% Quiz
30% Midterm
50% Final

Homework will be counted as long as you have handed them in. Quiz may be quite difficult but count little to the overall grading (there are four quizzes throughout).

Poor grading since midterm higher than mean and  final at mean but still no B range.

Cheatsheet is allowed at both midterm and final (half and one page, hand written).
sections.workload:
Homework are not too difficult as long as you have studied some and read the slides, not to mention that as long as you have handed in them the credits will be counted.
The textbooks can be found online, therefore it is best not to cramp all studying before finals. Can better understand the concepts if start studying early.
